research.title: Alignment Myopia in Generative AI
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current generative AI alignment relies on a myopic paradigm that prioritizes immediate conversational satisfaction. By relying on short-horizon feedback, this approach ignores the profound, longitudinal externalities of persistent human-AI interaction, which can lead to adverse outcomes. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Amortized Optimization for Calibrating Stochastic Social Simulators
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stochastic simulators need suitable parameter values to reproduce observed behaviour in complex systems. Searching for these values through repeated simulations makes frequent recalibration computationally expensive. We develop an amortized optimizer that uses simulations collected in advance. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Beyond accuracy: what AI assurance needs to establish in public services
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Public bodies increasingly rely on AI-produced evidence, including classifications, summaries and assessments. These outputs can inform policy decisions and service delivery, making their reliability a matter of public accountability. Establishing whether this evidence can be relied. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Beyond the principle-practice gap: Responsible AI as situated epistemic and ethical practice
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Responsible AI scholarship has found that ethical principles are frequently not reflected in AI design and development. Conceptualised as a `gap' between principle and practice, this is framed as a problem of implementation, awareness or compliance. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Building a Method: Challenges and Lessons from Developing an Impact Evaluation Framework for Public Investment in Open Source Software
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern societies and institutions depend on an invisible layer of open digital infrastructure: foundational, openly accessible digital technologies that support a broad range of social and economic activities. Open source software is a core component of. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Clear Human Web: Where a Person Vouches for Every Client
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: The web cannot tell whether a request comes from a person or from a program. Sites have checked the network address and puzzles in its place, and both have given way: automated traffic exceeds human traffic. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: InterSim: Innovative Intersection Digital Twins for Human-in-the-Loop Driving Simulation
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Innovative intersection designs can improve roadway safety and operational efficiency, but their uncommon geometries may create challenges for driver comprehension during early deployment. Evaluating these designs through full-scale field implementation can also be costly. This paper. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Measuring Risk, Not Harm: Detecting Psychological Harm Risk Factors in LLM Conversations
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Psychological harms from interactions with large language models cannot be monitored directly because they may emerge over repeated interactions and depend strongly on subjective individual user context. We propose measuring risk, not harm: detecting observable AI. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
